extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers) in the life sciences and medicine considering submission to eLife
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural standards describing how eLife conducts peer review by reviewing preprints and what outputs and choices are produced for authors. Intended to explain eligibility, roles, outputs, fees, and options (including a temporary traditional model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint-only eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We only review articles that have been made available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewed Preprints combine the advantages of preprints with the scrutiny offered by peer review; eLife's approach requires that the manuscript already be posted as a preprint before it will be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor selection by active researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors who are active researchers decide which preprints are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of preprints for review is made by editors who are themselves active researchers, indicating subject-matter expertise in the decision to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative review discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss the reviews with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process includes direct discussion among editors and reviewers to refine assessments and ensure coherent evaluation before publication of reviews and assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No accept/reject decision after peer review (Reviewed Preprint outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no accept/reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published on the eLife website as a Reviewed Preprint that includes an eLife assessment, public reviews, and a response from the authors (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of traditional accept/reject outcomes, the peer review produces transparent outputs (assessment, reviews, response) and the Reviewed Preprint is published on eLife's site.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limit on number reviewed or published
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we review or publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's model is explicitly not quota-limited — selection is based on editorial judgment of preprints rather than a cap on publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author option to convert to Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point following peer review, authors can choose to have their Reviewed Preprint published as a regular journal article (known as the Version of Record) to mark the end of the publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain control to request formal publication as a Version of Record after peer review, which finalises the publishing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee timing and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for publishing an article with eLife is $2,000, charged at the point we commit to peer reviewing the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $2,000 fee is charged when eLife commits to peer review (i.e., up-front at commitment), rather than at later publication milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funder open-access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of an eLife Version of Record complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's Version of Record meets funder mandates for immediate OA; additionally, an increasing number of funders recognise Reviewed Preprints in research assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife assessment output
rubrics_metrics.description: An eLife assessment that summarises the significance of the findings and the strength of the evidence; the editor and the reviewers write this assessment with the help of a common vocabulary to ensure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment aims to capture both importance and evidential strength, and uses a common vocabulary developed by eLife to promote consistency across assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews published alongside the Reviewed Preprint should make clear what the work does well, where it falls short, and explicitly assess whether the data justify the authors' claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for authors (not part of Reviewed Preprint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for the authors, including suggestions for revising and improving the article. These recommendations are not included in the Reviewed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewers provide suggestions to authors for improvement, those recommended revisions are separated from the public Reviewed Preprint record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary availability of traditional peer-review model
rubrics_metrics.description: The model of peer review described above was introduced in January 2023. For a limited period authors can ask for submissions to be reviewed under eLife’s traditional model (which includes an accept/reject decision after peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors have, for a limited transition period, the option to select the older traditional model that includes accept/reject outcomes rather than automatic publication as a Reviewed Preprint.
